title_ar: هل رأى الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه ؟
title_en: Did the Messenger, Peace and Blessings Be upon Him, See His Lord?
body_ar: الجواب: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن هذا السؤال فسأله أبو ذر عنه فقال «نور أنى أراه»، و قد رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الآية الكبرى في معراجه و رأى جبريل و رآه على صورته له ستمائة جناح ما بين جناحيه بين المشرق و المغرب،﴿و لقد رآه نزلة أخرى عند سدرة المنتهى عندها جنة المأوى﴾، و لكنه كلمه الله سبحانه و تعالى فسمع كلامه عز و جل.
body_en: The answer: the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked this very question — Abu Dharr asked him about it — and he said: 'Light; how should I see Him?' The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, did see the greatest sign on his night ascent (miʿrāj), and he saw Gabriel, and saw him in his own form, having six hundred wings, the span between two of his wings reaching from the east to the west: {And he certainly saw him at another descent, by the Lote Tree of the Furthest Boundary, near which is the Garden of Refuge} (Sūrat al-Najm 53:13–15). But God, glorified and exalted, spoke to him, and he heard His speech, mighty and majestic.

flags.arabic: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن هذا السؤال فسأله أبو ذر عنه فقال «نور أنى أراه» … و لكنه كلمه الله سبحانه و تعالى فسمع كلامه
flags.context: the whole answer, considered as a response to the title's question
options: render faithfully and mark that no categorical answer is stated
render as a denial that the Prophet saw his Lord
render as leaving the question undecided between the two positions
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The Sheikh never says in so many words that the Prophet did or did not see his Lord. He answers by quoting the Prophet's own reply to Abu Dharr, then lists what the Prophet did see — the greatest sign, and Gabriel in his form — and closes with what did take place, that God spoke to him and he heard His speech. The structure carries an implication, but the implication is his and not the translator's, and the English must not be allowed to state a conclusion he withheld. This is a long-disputed question between the Companions and among the theologians, and the Sheikh gives none of that disagreement here.

flags.context: the Prophet's reply to Abu Dharr, as the Sheikh quotes it
options: 'He is light; how could I see Him?'
'[I saw] light; how then should I see Him?'
flags.note: The Arabic is elliptical and has been read in all three of these ways by the commentators, with materially different consequences for the question being asked. The Sheikh quotes it without comment and without narrator, collection or grading, and none has been supplied. The English keeps the ellipsis rather than closing it.

flags.context: the Qur'anic verse quoted after the mention of seeing Gabriel
options: render with the referent left as the Arabic leaves it ('he saw him')
render with 'Him' capitalised as referring to God
flags.note: The referent of the pronoun in this verse is itself the substance of the classical dispute, and the Sheikh quotes the verse immediately after describing the Prophet's sight of Gabriel, which suggests how he reads it — but he does not say so. The English leaves the pronoun uncapitalised and unglossed, which preserves the ambiguity of the Arabic. A reviewer should confirm.
